top_choice_rationale: P001 pairs a sharp theoretical prediction (Kane and Mele: time-reversal-protected Z2 insulator with helical edge channels, no magnetic field) with a decisive measurement of quantised edge conductance (Molenkamp, HgTe/CdTe wells), confirmed independently over about two decades. The three-name allocation is stable, and a citation anchored on the two-dimensional quantum spin Hall state keeps it clear of the 2016 topological-phases prize. The omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang is a real weakness but is outweighed by the prediction-and-observation structure. P002 is next as a clean, bounded invention, although overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes is a risk. P003 and P004 follow because of attribution and overlap problems (Wineland 2012; Cirac, Jaksch and Dalibard credit) and unproven scalability or classical-simulability reach. Any of these is preferable to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no documented tie to any credited name. Field proximity only: my work is theoretical high-energy physics and cosmology, and I have no connection to Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, Katori, Ye, Cirac, Zoller, Blatt, Bloch or Greiner.
